verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. (1) A hard build failure on fixed H2 titles lets an edit in another repo stop the daily site deploy, and invites filler sections written only to pass. (2) The regex for 'minute' on every critical guide forces authors to invent durations. Only install has a measured one ('about 6-8 minutes'); a made-up '10 minutes' for notebook-requirements would be unverified text. (3) Making 'Next' a required heading duplicates G3. (4) The list of 'critical' slugs puts template pages in a site data file. That is tolerable only because it holds slugs, not text.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build a smaller check that does not stop deploys. Add `critical:` (slug list) to data/guides.yaml and a new scripts/lcsite/guide_shape.py with a pure `missing_sections(markdown, wanted)`. Require only three H2s on critical guides: 'What you need' (or 'Before you start'), 'Check that it worked' and 'If something does not work'. Drop the time regex and the Next heading. Report gaps from scripts/check_site.py and tests/test_guide_shape.py, naming the file and heading, in the same way warn_unlisted prints WARNING. Switch it to fail() only after the template pages comply (that is, after G2 is merged). Leave the whole-file check to the existing tests. Document the three headings in DESIGN.md under the guide pattern. Do not add a call in guides.py (258/300 lines). Include submit only as a plain content check on content/submit.md. Scope: install, initialise-repository, notebook-requirements, notebook-upload, executable-creation. The three plugin guides already use 'What you need' and 'If something does not work' (docs/guides/napari|fiji|qupath, H2 at lines 144 and 166, 169 or 166), so use that wording rather than inventing new. using-apps uses 'Something went wrong', which is a different wording. Repo: labconstrictor-site.
verdicts.evidence: No 'critical' in scripts/, tests/, data/, AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md (grep over those paths returned nothing). guides.py is 258 lines; describe() at line 96 only enforces a lead paragraph; tests/test_code_rules.py sets MAX_FILE_LINES=300 and MAX_FUNCTION_LINES=30. install.md already has a time sentence ('Installing takes about 6-8 minutes'), a lead and a Next section. warn_unlisted already prints WARNING rather than failing, so there is precedent for a softer check on template content. The three plugin guides' H2s were seen in docs/guides/*/index.md.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low-medium. Reading the first link of '## Next' as pager target is fragile: executable-creation's first link in '## 3. After the release' is install.md, which belongs to the Use track, so the pager would jump across tracks and break the Previous/Next symmetry. The proposed fallback to sidebar order is a second pager behaviour. It is acceptable only if DESIGN.md documents it. The auditor also treats installer-images and app-manifest as 'optional pages' in the way. They sit directly after initialise_repository in the template README because the form takes the images and the manifest values, so they are not obviously misplaced; moving them is an editorial choice for the template owners.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Fix the contradictions first with text and order, no generator change. In the template (LabConstrictor): add a short `## Next` pointing to the next task at the end of notebook_requirements.md (to notebook_upload), notebook_upload.md (to executable_creation) and initialise_repository.md (to the next step the owners choose); change install.md's Next so its first link matches the pager (point to the site's 'Open and use an app', via the absolute site URL as app_manifest.md already does for /submit/), or leave install's Next and reorder data/guides.yaml in labconstrictor-site so that Use-track order matches it. Make executable_creation.md's After the release list the last step of the From-zero path. Only if mismatches persist after that, consider the pager rule from the proposal, in a new module, limited to guides that have a `## Next` section, with the fallback documented in DESIGN.md and a build failure when the first Next link is not a guide in the same track. Reordering the template README is the owners' decision, not required by this gap. Repos: LabConstrictor (.tools/docs/*.md, README.md) and labconstrictor-site (data/guides.yaml, optionally guides.py).
verdicts.evidence: Built pager of install: Next is 'Open and use an app' (../using-apps/) while its '## Next' says 'Use notebooks after installation'. executable-creation pager Next is notebook-portability (the flat list leaves the From-zero section), while its text points to install and app-manifest. app-manifest pager Next is external-code-upload, while its text says 'Get listed' (submit). initialise-repository pager Next is installer-images. notebook-requirements and notebook-upload have no Next section (checked in the built Markdown). verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium for three of the sub-items. (1) 'Ctrl+C on every system' is almost certainly right for a macOS Terminal window (Cmd+C copies there) but nobody has verified it on this app; wording should be checked on a Mac before it is published. (2) Steps for changing installer images 'later' are undocumented anywhere I looked. The streamlit form writes images into app/logo and construct.yaml only during initialisation (app.py around lines 612-615). Writing steps for the later case would invent a procedure; the safer edit is to remove 'or at any time later' until someone verifies one. (3) The uninstall steps should come from the one sentence already on the page (`Settings > Apps > Installed apps`), not be invented.
verdicts.refined_proposal: In the template repo (LabConstrictor, .tools/docs/): (a) initialise_repository.md: turn the dense paragraph into a numbered list using only the existing facts (open the form; wake the app if it shows Zzzz via 'Yes, get this app back up!'; choose 'Start initialisation' under 'Initialise a repository'; fill in and submit; a PR is created; accept it per accept_pull_request.md). (b) notebook_usage.md: fix 'finnisehd' and 'LabConstrisctor'; reword the stop instruction to 'press Ctrl+C in the terminal window' only after checking on macOS. (c) troubleshooting_installed_app.md: replace the link to download_executable.md (17 lines, contains no uninstall steps, and it is in SKIP so it is not on the site) with the plain instruction 'Settings > Apps > Installed apps, select the app, Uninstall', which the same paragraph already names. (d) notebook_upload.md step 6: use the form's real label `🚀 Create pull request` (app.py:946, 961); accept_pull_request.md: 'Got to' becomes 'Go to'. (e) installer_images.md: do not add steps; either delete 'or at any time later' or have a maintainer confirm and document the later-change procedure first. These are separate small edits and independent of the G1 checker.
